target_customer: Banks, asset managers and digital-asset infrastructure providers that hold or move on-chain assets
problem: Financial institutions moving digital assets lack a live model of their on-chain exposure, so cyber risk, vendor and protocol diligence and pre-execution transaction checks are manual or fragmented.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API for risk assessment, policy generation and transaction screening, pricing not public
product_category: Blockchain security and on-chain risk platform for institutions

founders.name: Dan Danay
founders.background_notes: YC page says he served as a captain in the Israeli Navy.

founders.name: Isaac Grossman
founders.background_notes: Launch post describes him as a veteran of Matzov, Israel's cryptography unit. No formal education listed.

founders.name: Liran Kogan
prior_employers: Check Point (launched and led blockchain security products)
founders.background_notes: Degrees not specified on the YC page.

competitors.name: Hypernative
competitors.what: Pre-transaction screening and on-chain security, embedded in custody workflows
competitors.traction_then: Covers 75+ chains; integrated with Fireblocks, Safe and Utila per its own material (vendor claim)

competitors.name: Blockaid
competitors.what: Real-time risk infrastructure and screening API for institutions

competitors.name: Fireblocks with Chainalysis and Elliptic
competitors.what: Compliance suite bundling transaction monitoring, wallet screening and Travel Rule tooling

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs on-chain data ingestion, risk modelling and a pre-execution policy engine integrated with institutional wallets, but built on existing blockchain data and LLM tooling by a team that previously built similar products at Check Point.

defensibility.rationale: Institutional integrations and approved policies create some lock-in once deployed, but Hypernative, Blockaid and Fireblocks already sell overlapping pre-transaction screening, so the wedge is thin early on.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were already shipping pre-transaction checks and AI agents in spring 2026; no outcome yet because the company is new.

market_need_then: The July 2026 EU deadline for continuous on-chain monitoring cited by Hypernative, plus bank interest in digital assets, creates compliance demand. The company reports proofs of concept and bank evaluations, which are its own claims.

branding.domain_note: Uses verdictmachine.com, an exact-match domain; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: not described by any source seen
identity.visual_style: Evidence and control oriented, before and after use case blocks
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct, short declarative headlines aimed at risk committees and auditors

brand_strength.rationale: Brand search found no coverage of the name or logo; the company is weeks old.

outcome_analysis: Verdict Machine is an active Summer 2026 company with no exit and no reported shutdown, so the outcome is open. Its strongest asset is founder market fit, since two founders launched blockchain security at Check Point and one founded keyTango, but incumbents already sell pre-transaction screening and funding is not publicly confirmed.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k seed round with no investors named; it is a single aggregator figure and is unverified, so no round is recorded. The company site lists LayerZero, Trilitech and Codexa as customers; this is a company claim. No outcome news found.
